text:
sarah: Hi @people-ops — I lost my physical insurance card while traveling and have a specialist appointment in Lisbon tomorrow. I need something official to show the clinic. Is there a way to get a temporary proof of coverage same-day? Also I have a dependent (partner) on my plan who’s with me — will a digital card show both of us?

tony (Benefits): Hi Sarah — we can help. Short answer: yes, we can issue an internal benefits confirmation letter (policy number + member name + dependent names) that you can print or show on your phone. Typical turnaround is same day during business hours if you request via email with your last 4 of SSN and travel dates.

emma: Also check the carrier’s mobile app for a digital card/QR — many carriers push out a digital card immediately if youre already enrolled. But for international use the clinic may still ask for a policy phone number or a confirmation letter from us.

benefits-bot: Automated: To request an internal confirmation letter email benefits@redwood.com with subject line: "Temp ID Request - Sarah [lastname] - Lisbon". Include: 1) member full name; 2) last 4 SSN; 3) dependent full name(s) if you need them shown; 4) date of service/appointment. Standard turnaround: 1 business day; expedited same-day available if sent before 2pm PT.

sarah: The appointment is at 10:30 local tomorrow (~5am PT). Is there any chance of same-day if I email now? The clinic wants insurer phone and policy number printed on a form.

tony (Benefits): If you email now with the details we can issue an internal confirmation letter within a few hours today and include the carrier phone and policy code for international billing. If you need the carrier to accept direct billing, note that some clinics will still require the dependent to be on file with the carrier. For those cases we can also submit a request to the carrier to pre-authorize the dependent coverage for that date — but carrier response may not be same-day.

benefits-bot: Tip: If the clinic refuses direct billing and requires pre-authorization, bring the internal confirmation letter + screenshot of the carrier digital card. Our letter includes an internal case number so we can follow up with the clinic if needed.

emma: If you paid OOP and need reimbursement later, keep the itemized invoice with the clinic stamp, translation if not in English, and proof of payment (card statement). For currency conversions include a screenshot of the daily FX rate (xe.com or bank) for the service date.

sarah: One more twist: my partner is listed as a dependent but their name is spelled differently on their passport (accent vs no accent). Will that block the clinic?

ton y (Benefits): Small name diacritic differences rarely block verification but carriers sometimes insist on exact matches for dependent billing. In your case we can include both spellings on the internal confirmation letter (official name on file + alternate spelling) if you provide the partner's passport scan. Also bring ID and we can annotate the letter to avoid confusion.

hr-ops: FYI if you need proof of eligibility for visa/consulate purposes later we can also produce an employment+benefits verification letter but that’s separate — email hr-ops@redwood.com for that.

sarah: Thanks all. Ill email benefits now with last4 + appointment details + partner passport scan. Appreciate the quick help.

benefits-bot: Reminder: Attach PDF copies (not photos) when possible. If you need the carrier phone included in the letter, add "Include carrier phone" in the email subject.
